Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the State, who opposes the prayer for bail.

The petitioner is an accused for allegedly committing offence punishable under Sections 429, 406,
188, 120-B/34 of the Indian Penal Code, Sections 11(a)(d)(e)(i)(k) of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, Rule 3 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rule, 2001,
Section 55 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is alleged that some camels were confiscated before Bakrid, and were seized and entrusted to the petitioner.
The petitioner could not produce the said camels when there were directed to produce.
It is alleged that the petitioner had slaughtered the said animals.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he has falsely been implicated in this case.
He submits that the petitioner is in custody since 16.01.2017.
Keeping in view the period of custody, I am inclined to allow this application.

Accordingly, the petitioner, namely, Amin Ansari is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.
10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of A.C.J.M, Bermo at Tenughat, in connection with Nawadih, P.S. Case No. 69 of 2017, corresponding to G. R. No. 786 of 2017.
(Ananda Sen, J.) Amar/cp3 Amin Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand .....
